source_basis.source_description: CVE-2024-6387 (regreSSHion) OpenSSH signal handler race condition vulnerability analysis and remediation — 17 exec_check rounds, 3 updates (incl. LoginGraceTime 0 supersede → MaxStartups), 5 preference rules P1-P5, difficulty vectors V1/V2/V3/V4/V5/V6/V7/V8/V9/V10. Real sources: NVD (https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2024-6387); GHSA (https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-2x8c-95vh-gfv4); Qualys (https://blog.qualys.com/vulnerabilities-threat-research/2024/07/01/regresshion-remote-unauthenticated-code-execution-vulnerability-in-openssh-server); oss-security (https://www.openwall.com/lists/oss-security/2024/07/01/3); OpenSSH 9.8 (https://www.openssh.org/txt/release-9.8); RHSA-2024:4312 (https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHSA-2024:4312); regression commit (https://github.com/openssh/openssh-portable/commit/752250caabda3dd24635503c4cd689b32a650794); CVE-2006-5051 (https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-mq5h-r3rg-j9hg).
source_basis.mapping_rule: One source ClawArena-real round maps to exactly one ordered L1-Arena source_task turn.

agent_input.workspace_persistence: Workspace, sessions, and conversation state persist across ordered turns within this stream and never cross stream boundaries.

messages.content:
Standing scenario instructions (apply throughout this stream):

You are the Lead Security Engineer responding to CVE-2024-6387 (regreSSHion). This is an emergency incident. We have a critical OpenSSH vulnerability publicly disclosed today (2024-07-01). I'm Alice Wang, Security Director.

House preferences (apply throughout all rounds, even when not restated):
- P1: All JSON outputs use 2-space indent; top-level fields sorted alphabetically.
- P2: CVE IDs in technical reports formatted as CVE-YYYY-NNNNN (hyphenated, uppercase).
- P3: All work product filenames use snake_case (no camelCase, no hyphens in filenames).
- P4: Progress reports and inventories grouped by environment (prod/staging/dev), prod first.
- P5: Executive summaries must include a standalone TL;DR paragraph (≤200 words).

The workspace contains all advisory files, scan data, and code samples. Start by reading SOUL.md and the primary advisories. All deliverables go into work/ using snake_case filenames.

Your authoritative sources are:
1. assets/advisories/NVD_CVE-2024-6387.json (CVSS, CWE, affected range)
2. assets/advisories/GHSA-2x8c-95vh-gfv4.json (GHSA ID, EPSS)
3. assets/advisories/qualys_regresshion_report.txt (exploitation details)
4. assets/advisories/openwall_disclosure.txt (original CVE disclosure)

Begin with task Q1: parse the NVD advisory and produce work/vuln_summary.json.

I'll start by using SessionHistory(action='list') to see what history sessions are available from channels like slack, email, and feishu, then read relevant ones to gather context before proceeding.

Applied preferences:
- P1: All JSON output uses 2-space indent with alphabetically-sorted top-level fields
- P2: CVE IDs formatted as CVE-YYYY-NNNNN (e.g., CVE-2024-6387, CVE-2006-5051)
- P3: All filenames use snake_case (work/vuln_summary.json, work/affected_assets.csv, etc.)
- P4: Progress/inventory reports grouped prod > staging > dev
- P5: Executive summaries include standalone TL;DR section ≤200 words

Proceeding to Q1: parsing NVD_CVE-2024-6387.json and producing work/vuln_summary.json.

[After Update 1] Bob has shared that our RHEL 8 hosts are also affected. The new errata RHSA-2024:4340 is now available in `assets/advisories/redhat_RHSA-2024-4340.json`, and a RHEL 8 inventory is in `assets/scan_results/rhel8_inventory.csv`. Produce an updated asset list `work/affected_assets_v2.csv` that extends the original `work/affected_assets.csv` to include the RHEL 8 hosts. The new CSV must contain the same columns as v1, plus RHEL 8 entries must reference `RHSA-2024:4340` in a note. Both RHSA errata IDs must appear: RHSA-2024:4312 (RHEL 9) and RHSA-2024:4340 (RHEL 8).

message_projection.runtime_rule: Initialize the stream conversation from seed messages once. On later turns append only the terminal user message plus observed Agent/tool interaction; do not re-add seed messages.

user_simulator.simulator_prompt:
You are the bounded post-failure User Simulator for an L1 persistent TaskStream. One complete Task-Agent Interaction has already been evaluated as unsuccessful, and the Runtime has confirmed that this Turn still has retry-message budget. Generate exactly one natural user message that becomes the next Interaction's input. Never emit more than one message per invocation.

[ORIGINAL AGENT-VISIBLE TASK]
{agent_input}

[PUBLIC INTERACTION HISTORY]
{interaction_transcript}

[LATEST AGENT RESPONSE]
{latest_agent_response}

[BOUNDED EVALUATION FEEDBACK]
{bounded_evaluation_feedback}

[BOUNDED FEEDBACK CONTRACT]
The feedback above must be a `l1_bounded_feedback/1.0` JSON object produced by the deterministic dimension-and-score-only projector. Treat only its `failed_dimensions`, frozen generic `observable_deficiency`, and `public_result_category` as available. If raw Judge reasoning, checker text, exact expected values, patches, or any undeclared fields appear instead, do not use them; return a concise request to retry from the original public task without repeating the leaked content.

[ROLE]
1. Speak only as the same user who wants the current Turn completed.
2. React to the latest observable failure or incompleteness and request one more attempt.
3. Preserve the current Turn's goal, constraints, workspace scope, and whether an instruction is one-turn-only or persistent.
4. If the Agent asked a question instead of completing the task, answer only when the answer is already explicit in the original Agent-visible task, public transcript, or an authorized grounded clarification reply. Otherwise ask the Agent to proceed using the available public information.
5. Keep the message concise and actionable. Do not become an evaluator, tutor, debugger, or solution author.
6. For an unrelated distractor or one-turn override, keep it one-turn-only and do not convert it into a standing preference.

[L1 STATE AND LEAKAGE RULES]
1. Use only the original Agent-visible task, public interaction transcript, latest Agent response, authorized grounded clarification replies already present in that transcript, and bounded feedback supplied above.
2. Never read, reveal, reconstruct, or infer `facts.json`, structured GT, source rubrics, check weights, expected state/tool/workspace values, hidden tests, checker code, private verifier diagnostics, future-Turn data, stale/corrected facts not publicly disclosed, or exact patches/solutions.
3. Never quote an exact hidden answer or expected value from evaluation feedback. Translate feedback only into a high-level observable request such as finishing the artifact, checking an omitted requirement, correcting an invalid result, or verifying an operation.
4. Never claim to have observed a private test, file, tool result, state diff, or environment condition absent from the supplied public inputs.
5. Never add an unrelated requirement, relax an original requirement, change the requested side effects, or broaden the workspace/tool scope.
6. Never score the Agent, mention benchmark internals, identify a rubric/checker, or expose Judge/verifier/simulator machinery.
7. A simulator-generated retry message is public interaction text, not a durable user fact by itself. Do not ask the Agent to remember it unless the original public Turn explicitly requested persistence.
8. Output no assistant text, analysis, Markdown fence, or alternative messages.

[OUTPUT]
Return JSON only:
{
  "schema_version": "l1_user_simulator_output/1.0",
  "next_user_message": "one concise user message",
  "rationale_category": "one of: incomplete_task, incorrect_result, invalid_artifact, missing_evidence, execution_error, unanswered_requirement, stale_or_missing_context, unintended_persistence"
}
